cases.question: Where are sales reps' monthly quotas kept, and how does the rep sales report pull out the right month's figure?
cases.answer: The sales reps' monthly quotas are kept in the SalesRep table, in the MonthQuota field, which is a decimal extent 12 array (one element per month, January through December) [schema:SalesRep]. The rep sales report (rpt/rpt-repsales.p) pulls out the right month's figure by subscripting the MonthQuota array with the input parameter ip-month: `ASSIGN d-quota = SalesRep.MonthQuota[ip-month]` [corpus/rpt/rpt-repsales.p#main]. The report takes ip-month as an input parameter (1-12) and uses it both to filter ArHist records by MONTH(ArHist.InvoiceDate) and to index into the quota array.

cases.question: The rep sales monthly report gets slow as invoice history grows - is there an indexing problem in how it selects the records?
cases.answer: The rep sales monthly report [corpus/rpt/rpt-repsales.p#main] has an indexing problem. The report selects ArHist records using `WHERE ArHist.SalesRep = SalesRep.SalesRep AND MONTH(ArHist.InvoiceDate) = ip-month AND YEAR(ArHist.InvoiceDate) = ip-year`. The MONTH() and YEAR() functions in the WHERE clause prevent the InvoiceDate index from being used for bracketing, forcing a full table scan of every ArHist row for each sales rep. The ArHist table [schema:ArHist] has indexes on SalesRep and InvoiceDate, but the SalesRep index alone cannot filter by date, and the function calls on InvoiceDate disable that index. The code comment acknowledges this: "TODO: the MONTH()/YEAR() functions in the WHERE keep the InvoiceDate index from bracketing, so this walks every ArHist row per rep. Fine at our volumes. sw 2005". As invoice history grows, this becomes a performance problem.

cases.question: Which program invokes deallocate-item in the allocation manager, and for which order lines does it get called?
cases.answer:
Looking at the retrieved code, I can answer this question directly from what I've read.

The program **oe/oe-cancel.p** invokes `deallocate-item` in the allocation manager [corpus/oe/oe-cancel.p#main]. 

It gets called for order lines that have `OrderLineStatus = {&LIN-ORDERED}` (the "Ordered" status). The code iterates through all OrderLines of the order being cancelled, and for each line in Ordered status, it runs `deallocate-item IN gh-alloc` passing the ItemNum and Qty to release the inventory allocation back to available stock [corpus/oe/oe-cancel.p#main]. Backordered lines are skipped because they were never allocated in the first place.

cases.question: Can individual installations hook their own custom logic into the nightly order posting run, and how does that mechanism work?
cases.answer:
Looking at the retrieved code, I can see the answer in [corpus/oe/oe-post.p#main]. Let me verify I have all the information needed.

The code shows that oe-post.p defines a variable `c-exit-proc` initialized to "oe/oe-exit.p", and near the end of the posting transaction, there's a conditional RUN statement that checks if this file exists and runs it if found. The comment explicitly states this is "Site-specific posting exit. Deliberately NOT in source control - each site drops its own oe/oe-exit.p on the PROPATH."

I have read this unit and can answer the question completely from it.

Yes, individual installations can hook custom logic into the nightly order posting run. The mechanism works as follows:

After each order is successfully invoiced and its status is set to Posted, oe-post.p checks whether a file "oe/oe-exit.p" exists on the PROPATH using `SEARCH(c-exit-proc)`. If found, it runs that procedure with `RUN VALUE(c-exit-proc) (INPUT Order.OrderNum)`, passing the order number as input. This exit hook runs inside the same transaction as the invoice creation and status update, so if the hook fails, the entire order posting rolls back together. The comment explicitly notes this is "Site-specific posting exit. Deliberately NOT in source control - each site drops its own oe/oe-exit.p on the PROPATH."

cases.question: I ran ship confirmation on an order, but the header is still Ordered - what can leave it that way?
cases.answer:
Looking at the retrieved code, I can answer this question directly from [corpus/oe/oe-ship.p#main].

The ship confirmation procedure (oe-ship.p) only marks the order header as Shipped when there are no lines left in Ordered or Backordered status. Specifically, after shipping individual lines, it checks:

```
IF NOT CAN-FIND(FIRST OrderLine OF Order
                WHERE OrderLine.OrderLineStatus = {&LIN-ORDERED}
                   OR OrderLine.OrderLineStatus = {&LIN-BACKORD})
```

So the header stays "Ordered" if any line is still in Ordered or Backordered status. Lines can remain Ordered if:

1. The Item record is locked during ship-line processing - the line is "left open" with a message about the lock [corpus/oe/oe-ship.p#ship-line]
2. The Item record is missing/not available - the line is "left open" with a message about the missing item [corpus/oe/oe-ship.p#ship-line]
3. The line was already in Backordered status - the ship procedure only processes lines WHERE OrderLine.OrderLineStatus = {&LIN-ORDERED}, so backordered lines are skipped entirely [corpus/oe/oe-ship.p#main]

The notes in oe-ship.p confirm: "Backordered lines are NOT shipped and hold the order open; re-run after allocation catches up."

cases.question: When the nightly post runs, does it also relieve inventory for the orders it posts?
cases.answer:
Looking at the retrieved code, I can see that [corpus/oe/oe-post.p#main] is the nightly post procedure. Let me examine what it does regarding inventory relief.

The code shows a comment block from 04/17/2007 by dm stating "inventory relief moved OUT to oe-ship.p" and includes old commented-out code that used to relieve inventory. The comment explicitly says the old inventory relief code is "kept for reference."

The actual active code in oe-post.p does NOT relieve inventory - it only:
1. Validates order/line status
2. Calls ar/ar-invoice.p to create invoices
3. Changes Order.OrderStatus to Posted
4. Runs an optional exit hook

The inventory relief now happens in [corpus/oe/oe-ship.p#ship-line], which is called during shipping (before posting). That procedure decrements Item.OnHand and Item.Allocated when lines are shipped.

So the answer is clear from the code and comments.

**Answer:**

No, the nightly post does NOT relieve inventory. Inventory relief was moved out of oe-post.p to oe-ship.p in April 2007. The posting procedure [corpus/oe/oe-post.p#main] now only invoices shipped orders (via ar/ar-invoice.p) and marks them Posted. The actual inventory relief - decrementing Item.OnHand and Item.Allocated - happens earlier during shipping in [corpus/oe/oe-ship.p#ship-line], which updates the Item record directly when each line ships.

cases.question: After an order line is created, which procedures can later change its line status, and what values do they set?
cases.answer:
After an order line is created, two procedures can change its line status:

1. **oe/oe-cancel.p** sets OrderLineStatus to "Cancelled" ({&LIN-CANCELLED}) when cancelling an order [corpus/oe/oe-cancel.p#main].

2. **oe/oe-ship.p** (specifically its ship-line internal procedure) sets OrderLineStatus to "Shipped" ({&LIN-SHIPPED}) when shipping allocated lines [corpus/oe/oe-ship.p#ship-line].

Note that oe-entry.p#add-order-line sets the initial status at creation time (either "Ordered" or "Backordered"), but does not change it afterward [corpus/oe/oe-entry.p#add-order-line].

cases.question: If a customer is only slightly over their credit limit, will order entry still decline the order?
cases.answer:
I can answer this question from the retrieved code. The credit check procedure includes a tolerance that allows orders slightly over the credit limit.

In [corpus/oe/oe-credit.p#main], a variable `d-tolerance` is defined with an initial value of 100. The comment notes this was "added after the Meyer's Hardware escalation. Do not remove."

The actual credit decision in [corpus/oe/oe-credit.p#check-credit] compares the customer's balance plus open order exposure against their credit limit **plus this tolerance**. The condition is:

```
IF sb-cust.Balance + get-open-balance() > sb-cust.CreditLimit + d-tolerance
```

This means if a customer is over their credit limit by 100 or less (the tolerance amount), the order will still be approved. Only if they exceed the limit by more than 100 will the order be declined.
